title: Teacher transfers: equalizing deficits across schools
extended_summary:
This paper studies a theoretical teacher-reassignment problem motivated by India’s Right to Free and Compulsory Education Act (RTE) and related state policies on redeploying teachers from surplus schools to deficit schools. The central question is how to reassign teachers so that post-transfer school deficits are reduced in a way that is fair, efficient, and strategy-proof.

The authors model the situation as a network flow problem in which each surplus school has a limited surplus of teachers, each teacher has an acceptable set of deficit schools, and each deficit school has a maximum number of teachers it can receive. A transfer is feasible only if it respects individual rationality for teachers and surplus schools, and no fractional transfers are allowed. The planner evaluates outcomes only by the post-transfer deficit vector, with the goal of equalizing deficits across schools.

Using convex cooperative game theory and the Megiddo-Dutta-Ray algorithm, the paper proves that a Lorenz-dominant post-transfer deficit vector always exists. Because the algorithm initially yields a fractional solution, the authors develop a second-stage rounding procedure via an auxiliary max-flow network to recover an integral transfer that preserves Lorenz dominance. They also show that a fixed tie-breaking version of the mechanism is strategy-proof for teachers. Extensions cover transfers between surplus schools and subject-specific teacher specializations.
